newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-UKRAINE IN "GOOD MOOD" BEFORE GERMAN MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UKRAINE IN "GOOD MOOD" BEFORE GERMAN MATCH.

text.p: World Cup group nine leaders Ukraine face European champions Germany in Kiev on Saturday in a match which could decide their chance of reaching next year's finals in France.
Though Ukraine head the group with 13 points from seven games from Germany on 11 from five matches and Portugal on nine from six, they are missing eight players through injury.
National coach Jozhef Sabo said he wanted to offer a debut to a ninth player, only to discover he was injured too.
Nevertheless, Sabo said morale in the team was high. "The mood is good and everyone wants to play.
"We are approaching this match very seriously. Can we play the German team? Yes, we can. Can we beat the German team? Yes, we can. It will be very tough, but we will try."
Those who will miss the match include top Dynamo Kiev midfielder Vitaly Kosovsky, who was facing surgery on a leg injury on Friday.
German coach Berti Vogts, meanwhile, has still not decided who should team up with captain Juergen Klinsmann in attack.
Vogts is divided between Oliver Bierhoff from Udinese Calcio or the Bundesliga's top scorer from Bayer Leverkusen, Ulf Kirsten, who is suffering from a slightly bruised rib.
Bochum's Dariusz Wosz replaces Andreas Moeller, who helped Borussia Dortmund to victory in the European Cup final last week, but now has a knee injury.

European Footballer of the Year Matthias Sammer from Borussia Dortmund is also set to return to the squad, but Stefan Reuter, suffering from muscular problems, will be replaced on the right by Dortmund team mate Joerg Heinrich.

Ukraine: 1-Oleksander Shovkovsky; 2-Oleh Luzhny, 3-Yuri Dmytrulin, 4-Oleksander Golovko, 5-Vladyslav Vashchuk; 6-Dmytro Mykhailenko, 7-Serhiy Nahornyak, 8-Yuri Kalitvintsev, 9-Hennady Zubov; 10-Andriy Shevchenko, 11-Serhiy Rebrov.

Germany (from): Andreas Koepke, Matthias Sammer, Juergen Kohler, Thomas Helmer, Joerg Heinrich, Dieter Eilts, Christian Ziege, Mario Basler, Dariusz Wosz, Ulf Kirsten Oliver Bierhoff, Juergen Klinsmann.
